## What's Changed

### Security fixes

This release fixes seven vulnerabilities. See [Security advisories: multiple vulnerabilities in Regexp and String case conversion](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/11/18/multiple-vulnerabilities-in-regexp-and-string/) for details.

* [GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5): Heap buffer overflow in case conversion of strings ([#20005](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/20005))
* [GHSA-7x2q-68qv-6p8x](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-7x2q-68qv-6p8x): Double free in regular expression compilation ([#20001](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/20001))
* [GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px): Integer overflow in case conversion of strings ([#20006](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/20006))
* [GHSA-wpqw-5qxg-m68r](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-wpqw-5qxg-m68r): Out-of-bounds read in case-insensitive regular expression matching ([#20002](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/20002))
* [GHSA-3p8q-wmhx-vm2w](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-3p8q-wmhx-vm2w): Heap buffer overflow in regular expression compilation ([#20000](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/20000))
* [GHSA-7whj-cfh7-xgm4](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-7whj-cfh7-xgm4): Heap buffer overflow in Regexp#to_s ([#20004](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/20004))
* [GHSA-pvgc-g7gj-pv6h](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-pvgc-g7gj-pv6h): Out-of-bounds read in case-insensitive backreference matching ([#20003](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/20003))

### String and encodings

* IO#write of a shareable String from multiple Ractors causes use-after-free ([Bug #22382](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/22382), [#19023](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/19023))
* String#initialize(encoding:) stores an inflated capacity and writes past the malloc'd buffer on append (rb_str_init termlen double-adjust) ([Bug #22423](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/22423), [#19297](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/19297), [#19403](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/19403))
* Coderange may be set incorrectly when concatenating a string into itself ([Bug #22451](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/22451), [#19357](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/19357))
* Use-after-free in `String` formatting with wide character encodings ([Bug #22461](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/22461), [#19472](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/19472))
* UTF-32 strings with a byte 0x80 or more in the most significant position are reported as valid ([Bug #22495](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/22495), [#19646](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/19646))
* Some String methods return a UTF-16/32 string without room for its terminator ([Bug #22517](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/22517), [#19794](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/19794))
* String#unpack("m") computes the buffer size with an overflowing multiplication ([Bug #22518](https://bugs.ruby-lang.org/issues/22518), [#19797](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/19797))
* Fix an out-of-bounds write in substrings of UTF-16/UTF-32 strings and an over-read when marking temporary buffers; only these two memory fixes are taken from “gc.c: Verify provided size in `rb_gc_impl_free`” by byroot ([#15989](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/15989))
* Copy terminator when moving strings to the heap. by eightbitraptor ([#16201](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/16201))
* Packing the buffer into itself is not possible by nobu ([#16741](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/16741))
* sprintf.c: Fix width overflow by nobu ([#17221](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/17221))
* Use the result encoding for the terminator in String#ljust/rjust/center by mame ([#17260](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/17260))
* Fix a potential out-of-bounds read by nobu ([#17754](https://github.com/ruby/ruby/pull/17754))

# What is Ruby?

Ruby is an interpreted object-oriented programming language often
used for web development. It also offers many scripting features
to process plain text and serialized files, or manage system tasks.
It is simple, straightforward, and extensible.

## Features of Ruby

* Simple Syntax
* **Normal** Object-oriented Features (e.g. class, method calls)
* **Advanced** Object-oriented Features (e.g. mix-in, singleton-method)
* Operator Overloading
* Exception Handling
* Iterators and Closures
* Garbage Collection
* Dynamic Loading of Object Files (on some architectures)
* Highly Portable (works on many Unix-like/POSIX compatible platforms as
  well as Windows, macOS, etc.) cf.
    https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master/maintainers_md.html#label-Platform+Maintainers

## How to get Ruby

For a complete list of ways to install Ruby, including using third-party tools
like rvm, see:

https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/downloads/

You can download release packages and the snapshot of the repository. If you want to
download whole versions of Ruby, please visit https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/downloads/releases/.

### Download with Git

The mirror of the Ruby source tree can be checked out with the following command:

    $ git clone https://github.com/ruby/ruby.git

There are some other branches under development. Try the following command
to see the list of branches:

    $ git ls-remote https://github.com/ruby/ruby.git

You may also want to use https://git.ruby-lang.org/ruby.git (actual master of Ruby source)
if you are a committer.

## Mailing list

There is a mailing list to discuss Ruby. To subscribe to this list, please
send the following phrase:

    join

in the mail subject (not body) to the address [ruby-talk-request@ml.ruby-lang.org].

[ruby-talk-request@ml.ruby-lang.org]: mailto:ruby-talk-request@ml.ruby-lang.org?subject=join

## Copying

See the file [COPYING](rdoc-ref:COPYING).

## Feedback

Questions about the Ruby language can be asked on the [Ruby-Talk](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/community/mailing-lists) mailing list
or on websites like https://stackoverflow.com.

Bugs should be reported at https://bugs.ruby-lang.org. Read ["Reporting Issues"](https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master/contributing/reporting_issues_md.html) for more information.

## Contributing

See ["Contributing to Ruby"](https://docs.ruby-lang.org/en/master/contributing/contributing_md.html), which includes setup and build instructions.

## The Author

Ruby was originally designed and developed by Yukihiro Matsumoto (Matz) in 1995.
